# dsh version manager

A Harness bundle that adds a **版本管理 / Versions** entry to the left navigation
and a panel with three

areas behind a segmented switcher. Only the open area is
rendered; a single status line under the s

witcher describes what that area runs
and what it has installed. The area this process runs from com

es first; the
remaining areas default to npm, npx, desktop:

- **npm** — the globally installed dsh (`npm install -g`), upgradeable but never
deletable.
- **npx*

* — the npx cache installs, listing the newest rc and alpha first, then
every other installed versio

n, which can be upgraded or deleted.
- **desktop** — the official desktop client: its installed vers

ion (read from the
Windows uninstall registry), the published version parsed from the installer
file
name, the installer facts, and a one-click install/upgrade.

The status line separates the version this process **runs** from what is merely
installed. The runni

ng version is read from the package that owns
`process.argv[1]` when the Host module loads — never f

rom the newest copy on
disk. Because an npx upgrade installs side by side and leaves the current
pro

cess alone, the panel can say `running 0.2.2-alpha.2 · newest installed
0.2.2-alpha.3` and offer to

restart onto the newer copy. The row badge
`running` follows the `_npx/<hash>` the process booted fr

tart onto the newer copy. The row badge
`running` follows the `_npx/<hash>` the process booted from.

Each CLI area shows two rows: the newest published **rc** and the newest published
**alpha**. Becaus

e npx installs do not overwrite each other, rc and alpha sit side
by side, so each row is judged aga

inst the newest installed version **of its own
channel** — an installed alpha never hides an rc that

is newer than the installed

## Desktop client
The official installers are fixed URLs with no version in the file name:

- Windows: `https://download.deepseek.com/desktop/dsh-latest-windows-x64.exe`
- macOS (Apple Silicon

): `https://download.deepseek.com/desktop/dsh-latest-macos-arm64.dmg`
- macOS (Intel): `https://down
load.deepseek.com/desktop/dsh-latest-macos-x64.dmg`

The panel shows the installed desktop build and the published version parsed
from the installer's `C

ontent-Disposition` file name (the fixed URL itself has no
version), plus the installer's size and r

elease date from a `HEAD` request.
Windows and the Apple Silicon DMG return a versioned file name; t

he current Intel
x64 DMG returns no `Content-Disposition`, so that platform shows “latest version
un

available” and does not light an update dot. The check is platform-neutral: if
the x64 artifact star

ts returning the header, the next check picks up its
version and the dot/UI work without a code chan

ge. Windows reads the uninstall
registry (`DisplayName` matching DeepSeek/dsh); macOS reads the
`CFB

undleShortVersionString` of `DeepSeek*.app` bundles in `/Applications` and
`~/Applications`, using `

plutil` for a binary plist. An x64 node running under
Rosetta still selects the ARM64 disk image, be

cause the machine is ARM64. A
published version newer than the installed one lights the desktop tab

and the
sidebar `new` marker; opening the desktop tab acknowledges that published
version.
Installing is deliberately two-step and never silent:

1. The panel asks the user to pick a folder through the Host-native directory
picker. Cancelling sto

ps the flow before anything is downloaded.
2. The Host downloads the official installer into that fo

lder, then launches it
so the user drives the installer UI. On macOS `open` mounts the `.dmg` for
th
e user to drag the app into `/Applications`.

Only `download.deepseek.com` is accepted, and only the fixed URL above is used —
the browser cannot

supply a download target. A failed download deletes its
partial file.
## Desktop shortcut

The toolbar's **桌面快捷方式 / Desktop shortcut** button writes a launcher to
the user's Desktop. It follo

ws **how this session was started**, not which
client happens to be installed: a machine with the de

sktop exe installed but
running from npx gets an npx launcher. Detection reads the process arguments

(`_npx/<hash>` marks an npx run, an Electron runtime marks the desktop app,
a path under a global `

node_modules` root marks npm); the remaining kinds are
fallbacks when the running install cannot be

ules` root marks npm); the remaining kinds are
fallbacks when the running install cannot be reached:

1. the kind that started this process,
2. then the desktop client,
3. then the global npm install,
4
. then an installed npx copy, preferring the directory this process runs from.

On Windows the launcher is `DeepSeek Harness.lnk`, targeting the desktop exe,
the global `%APPDATA%\

npm\dsh.cmd`, or an npx `.bin\dsh.cmd`. On macOS a CLI
install gets `DeepSeek Harness.command`, a `/

bin/sh` script that execs the
current node with the install's `lib/bin.js` and the preserved profile

arguments; the desktop client gets a `DeepSeek Harness.app` symlink to the
installed bundle. A `.co

mmand` uses Terminal's icon; the app symlink keeps the
app's own icon.

On Windows the shortcut uses the original glossy `assets/tray.ico` shipped with
this plugin (overrid

e with `DSH_VERSION_MANAGER_ICON`). It was rebuilt from the
original `icon.png` / `tray.ico` artwork

as a multi-size `.ico` (BMP frames plus
a 256 px PNG). Before writing the `.lnk`, the Host copies t

## What it scans

Every existing npm cache root is inspected (`npm_config_cache`,
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache`, `%APPDAT
A%\npm-cache`, `~/.npm`):

- `_npx/<hash>/package.json` → the installed dsh version, directory footprint,
and last-modified tim

e of the install.
- `_cacache/index-v5` → every `@deepseek-ai/dsh` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`
tarball

entry, aggregated per dsh version, including versions whose `_npx`
directory the user deleted by han

d (shown as **仅缓存 / cache only**).
- Globally installed `@deepseek-ai/dsh` packages are the npm area

. Windows
checks `%APPDATA%
pm
ode_modules` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%
pm
ode_modules`;
macOS and Linux

also check the running node's prefix
(`<prefix>/lib/node_modules`), `/usr/local`, `~/.npm-global`,

and the
nvm/nodebrew/Volta/asdf/fnm version roots; macOS additionally checks
`/opt/homebrew/lib/node

m/nodebrew/Volta/asdf/fnm version roots; macOS additionally checks
`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules`.
